explanation: A slot change raises or lowers the arm angle at release. Spin direction follows the slot: real pitchers who changed slots moved their spin direction about 0.9° per degree (and how far it rode over or ran under the slot only about a third as much, test T1).

So this keeps the pitcher's natural spin (spin rate, efficiency, velocity, and seam effect) and turns the spin direction one for one with the slot (Physics). A lower slot turns the spin toward the arm side: less ride, more run. What-If adds a Data-Driven range from real slot changes.
Release height moves too: about 0.3 in per degree, from 1,403 season-to-season slot changes by real pitchers.

Pitchers from there with this spin are real fastballs thrown from about that slot with similar spin for the speed, efficiency, and spin relative to the slot. Their results show what this kind of fastball does from there. Estimates, not promises.
